title: Playbook Execution Monitoring
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Playbook Execution Monitoring' only. Does not supplant organization-wide SIEM playbooks for unrelated threat classes or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `soc_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `security_infra_playbook_execution_monitoring` (UC-10.7.4), SOC dashboard panel "Security Infra — Playbook Execution Monitoring", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:soc_controls.

description: Detects risk tied to Playbook, Execution, Monitoring through UC-10.7.4 on `index=phantom_playbook_run`. Summarises `count` grouped by `playbook` across `the scheduled window` before applying `success_rate` < 95. Operators tune 'Playbook Execution Monitoring' using UC-10.7.4 runbook steps.
value: Tracking `activity` via UC-10.7.4 on `phantom_playbook_run` feeds improves response to 'Playbook Execution Monitoring' and reduces missed threat campaigns, control regressions, and SOC SLA breaches.
implementation: Turn on SOAR forwarding of the Playbook run data type to the phantom_playbook_run index. Track playbook success/failure rates; `playbook` is the playbook ID (open it in SOAR to see the name). Alert on failures for critical playbooks. Identify failing action steps for debugging in phantom_action_run. Report on automation coverage and time savings.
visualization: Table (playbook success rates), Bar chart (failure rate by playbook), Line chart (execution trend), Single value (overall success %).
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Maintenance window on `phantom_playbook_run` (UC-10.7.4)** — Planned work for 'Playbook Execution Monitoring' shifts `count` over `span=1h` while `playbook` remains in-scope.  Cross-check CMDB CHG.

2. **Batch `count` on `phantom_playbook_run`** — Scheduled automation elevates `success_rate` without crossing `success_rate` < 95 for UC-10.7.4. Compare `_time` minute against the job schedule.

3. **Synthetic probe on `playbook`** — Health checks in `phantom_playbook_run` populate the same fields the SPL groups on. Exclude monitoring-tagged assets before paging.

4. **Onboarding burst for `phantom_playbook_run`** — First 48h baseline for UC-10.7.4 on `playbook` is unstable; window via `soc_exception_register.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** `soc_exception_register.csv` keyed on `playbook`, `exception_reason`, `valid_until`.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk SOAR.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=phantom_playbook_run` (Splunk SOAR playbook run records forwarded by a SOAR forwarder group: id, playbook (playbook ID), container, status = success, failed, pending or running, start_time, update_time).
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Turn on SOAR forwarding of the Playbook run data type to the phantom_playbook_run index. Track playbook success/failure rates; `playbook` is the playbook ID (open it in SOAR to see the name). Alert on failures for critical playbooks. Identify failing action steps for debugging in phantom_action_run. Report on automation coverage and time savings.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=phantom_playbook_run
| stats count(eval(status="success")) as success, count(eval(status="failed")) as failed by playbook
| eval success_rate=round(success/(success+failed)*100,1)
| where success_rate < 95
```

Understanding this SPL

**Playbook Execution Monitoring** — SOAR playbook failures leave incidents unhandled. Monitoring ensures automation reliability and identifies integration issues.

Documented **Data sources**: `index=phantom_playbook_run` (Splunk SOAR playbook run records forwarded by a SOAR forwarder group: id, playbook (playbook ID), container, status = success, failed, pending or running, start_time, update_time). **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk SOAR. The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: phantom_playbook_run.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=phantom_playbook_run. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by playbook** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions (useful for per-host, per-user, or per-entity comparisons for this use case).
• `eval` defines or adjusts **success_rate** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.
• Filters the current rows with `where success_rate < 95` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare with the source-of-truth console (cloud CSP, EDR, or IdP) when the data allows it. Check the Splunk Security Essentials catalog for the same detection name, and review the ES Incident Review queue for related notables. Verify key fields, time windows, and index access for your search role.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Table (playbook success rates), Bar chart (failure rate by playbook), Line chart (execution trend), Single value (overall success %).

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Create the phantom_playbook_run events index on the indexers, then turn on a SOAR forwarder group that sends the Playbook run data type (see the forwarder-group artifact). Grant the search role access to phantom_playbook_run.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`playbook, success_rate`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: confirm the forwarder group is enabled in SOAR Forwarder Settings with the Playbook run data type selected, and that the phantom_playbook_run index exists on the indexers. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone.

productArtifacts.body:
On the Splunk platform, create the events index for each data type below before you turn on forwarding.

In Splunk SOAR: Home > Administration > Administration Settings > Forwarder Settings > + New Group
Name: a name for the group (not "splunk")
Token: the TCP token, if your Splunk deployment requires one
Indexers: the address of each indexer
Data types: Playbook run (index phantom_playbook_run)
Enabled: on
